newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak blue chips weaker, SAX eases from yr-high.
newsitem.headline: Slovak blue chips weaker, SAX eases from yr-high.

text.p: Major Slovak shares closed mostly weaker in thinner trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) on Monday, pulling the SAX index down 2.49 points to 206.15.

The biggest net loser on the listed floor was steel producer VSZ, falling 23 crowns to 712. Drug producer Slovakofarma fell 50 crowns to 5,100 crowns while oil refiner Slovnaft closed unchanged at 1,000 and oil and gas storage company Nafta closed down one crown at 1,670.
Overall volume fell to 546,514 shares from 3,191,891 stocks traded on Friday, while turnover decreased to 383.55 million crowns, from 5.39 billion crowns.
"We expected VSZ to fall, as the price had been artficially pushed up to prepare (price) levels for a sale of a larger package of the stock," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings.
Last Friday, brokers said, a domestic investor sold about 350,000 VSZ shares abroad for 740 crowns.
Dealers said the sale of VSZ shares was an example of how easily it was possible to manipulate prices with trading small volumes.

"This is a typical example...a domestic stock-holder, who wants to sell larger package, trades small volumes each time at higher price, and this prepares the designed price for the final sale," Sykora said.
Other blue chips traded insignificant volumes to indicate longer-term development, brokers said.
"There is still demand for blue chips, but this does not seem strong enough to pull the market significantly higher.
Sykora said foreign investors now consider the shares a bit too expensive adding the market should hold stable at current levels in the mid-term.
